data.name: Linus

in_hebrew.name: לינוס
in_hebrew.meaning: פירוש השם לינוס הוא כפלין או שזר
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם לינוס נגזר מהמילה היוונית λῖνος (linos), שפירושה פשתן או שזר. אין אזכור לשם זה בתנ"ך העברי, אך הוא מופיע בשם של אחד מהאפיפיורים הראשונים של הכנסייה הקתולית, לינוס האפיפיור, שהיה האפיפיור השני של הכנסייה והוא מוזכר בברית החדשה (האפיפיור לינוס היה אחד מתלמידיו של פטרוס). השם לינוס משמש גם כשם פרטי בקרב הנוצרים, ומשמעותו היא 'פשתן' או 'שזר', ויש לו קשרים רבים עם המסורת הנוצרית.

in_greek.name: Λίνος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Λίνος προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη λῖνος (linos), που σημαίνει ίνα ή λινό. Στην ελληνική παράδοση, ο Λίνος θεωρείται γιος του Απόλλωνα και της Ψάμαθης, και ήταν ποιητής και μουσικός. Στο Χριστιανισμό, ο Λίνος είναι γνωστός ως ο δεύτερος Επίσκοπος της Ρώμης και αναφέρεται στη Β΄ Πέτρου 2:13-14 και στην Α΄ Τιμόθεο 4:21.

in_latin.name: Linus
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Linus is derived from the Latinized form of the Greek name Λῖνος (Linos), meaning flax or thread. In Christian tradition, Linus was the second bishop of Rome and is mentioned in the New Testament (2 Timothy 4:21). The name Linus has been used in various Christian cultures and is associated with the Latin word for flax, 'linum', signifying purity and spiritual growth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Linus has its roots in Roman mythology and was most notably associated with Linus, a shepherd and teacher who played a significant role in the development of the legendary hero Heracles (Hercules). This early exposure to Linus not only instilled a strong connection to the classical past but also influenced the naming trend towards mythological and biblical names, making Linus a name of antiquity. Over time, Linus has appeared often in various works of literature and art as a name for musical prodigies, reflecting the cultural value and influence of music.
data.spiritual_significance: In a Christian context, the name Linus holds spiritual significance as it is linked to St. Linus, who is believed to have been bishop of Rome around 67 AD, during the time when St. Peter was a prisoner in Rome. Tradition holds that St. Linus was martyred for his faith, making his name an inspiration for those facing adversity and standing strong in their belief. Moreover, the Linus teaching tradition is integral in American culture, with Linus van Pelt, a Peanuts comic strip character who often shares his knowledge and wisdom, reflecting the importance of education and sharing the gospel message.

historical_references.reference: Linus was a Roman slave who was believed to have been freed by Saint Augustine of Hippo. Linus is venerated as a saint in the Roman Catholic Church and is the patron saint of musicians, music teachers, mathematicians, and students.
Linus was also a disciple of Saint Paul, mentioned in the New Testament in the Acts of the Apostles (16:2) as being with Paul during his first visit to Thessalonica, Greece.

modern_usage.modern_context: Linus Torvalds is a renowned figure in the technology industry, best known for creating the Linux operating system. His influence extends beyond just operating systems - he is a strong advocate for open source software development and innovation. Today, Linus is also associated with GitHub, the popular web-based platform for version control using Git. Additionally, he serves as the project manager for the Apache HTTP Server, one of the most widely used web servers worldwide.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Grace Linus in New York, United States credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Linus, which means "Linen cloth". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Linus is derived from the Latin word "linum," meaning "flax" or "linen." In Christian tradition, Linus represents humility, as he was the first to weave the robe for the infant Christ. This connection to cloth and weaving symbolizes the transformation of simple materials into something sacred and precious.
